title: Your Income Tax Return (ITR) for FY 2025-26: Deadlines & What's New
description: The deadline to file your Income Tax Return (ITR) for the Financial Year (FY) 2025-26 (Assessment Year 2026-27) is approaching. Most salaried individuals and .

faq.q: What is the basic exemption limit for individuals for FY 2025-26?
faq.a: Under the old tax regime, the basic exemption limit for individuals below 60 years is ₹2.5 lakh. For those aged 60 to 80, it's ₹3 lakh, and for those above 80, it's ₹5 lakh. Under the new tax regime, the basic exemption limit is ₹3 lakh for all individuals.

faq.q: What is Form 16 and why is it important?
faq.a: Form 16 is a certificate issued by your employer that provides details of the salary paid to you and the tax (TDS) deducted from your salary during the financial year. It is crucial for salaried individuals to file their ITR as it contains income and TDS details.

faq.q: Can I file my ITR after the due date?
faq.a: Yes, you can file a "belated return" after the due date, but it will attract a late filing fee under Section 234F (₹1,000 or ₹5,000, depending on your income). You also lose the ability to carry forward certain losses and may face interest on unpaid tax.

faq.q: What if I choose the old tax regime this year?
faq.a: The new tax regime is the default from the Income Tax Act 2025. If you wish to opt for the old tax regime to claim various deductions and exemptions, you must explicitly choose it while filing your ITR. For those with business income, this might involve submitting Form 10-IEA.

faq.q: Where can I find the official ITR forms?
faq.a: The official ITR forms for AY 2026-27 will be available on the Income Tax Department's e-filing portal (www.incometax.gov.in). It's important to use the latest forms for the correct assessment year.
